questions.q: What did the heads of the fathers of the Levites ask Eleazar, Joshua, and the heads of the Israelite tribes at Shiloh?
questions.a: They asked for cities to dwell in, with their pasturelands for their livestock, as Yahweh had commanded by the hand of Moses.

questions.q: How did the sons of Israel give cities and pasturelands to the Levites from their inheritance?
questions.a: The sons of Israel gave these cities and their pasturelands to the Levites by lot from their inheritance, just as Yahweh had commanded by the hand of Moses.

questions.q: How many cities in total, from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, were given by lot to the sons of Aaron the priest?
questions.a: All the cities of the sons of Aaron, the priests, were 13 cities and their pasturelands.

questions.q: How many cities in total, from Ephraim, Dan, and half-Manasseh, were given to the remaining clans of the sons of Kohath?
questions.a: There were ten cities in all, together with their surrounding fields, that these other clans that were descendants of Kohath received.

questions.q: How many cities in total, from half-Manasseh (in Bashan), Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, were given to the clans of Gershon?
questions.a: Altogether, the Gershonite clans received 13 cities, together with their surrounding fields.

questions.q: How many cities in total, from Zebulun, Reuben, and Gad, were given by lot to the clans of Merari, the remaining Levites?
questions.a: In all, this last group of Levite clans, the ones that were descendants of Merari, received 12 cities when the Israelite leaders cast lots for them.

questions.q: How many cities in total, with their pasturelands, did the Levites receive in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel?
questions.a: All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel were 48 cities and their pasturelands.

questions.q: What did Yahweh give to Israel from all around, according to all he had sworn to their fathers, and what happened to their enemies?
questions.a: Yahweh gave rest to them from all around, according to all that he had sworn to their fathers. None of their enemies were able to fight against them and defeat them. Instead, Yahweh helped Israel defeat all their enemies.

commentary.text: The cities allotted to the Levites.
God gave the land and rest to the Israelites, according to his promise.

Verses 1–8 The Levites waited till the other tribes were provided for, before they preferred their claim to Joshua. They build their claim upon a very good foundation; not their own merits or services, but the Divine precept. The maintenance of ministers is not a thing left merely to the will of the people, that they may let them starve if they please; they which preach the gospel should live by the gospel, and should live comfortably. (Jos 21:9-42)

By mixing the Levites with the other tribes, they were made to see that the eyes of all Israel were upon them, and therefore it was their concern to walk so that their ministry might not be blamed. Every tribe had its share of Levites' cities. Thus did God graciously provide for keeping up religion among them, and that they might have the word in all parts of the land. Yet, blessed be God, we have the gospel more diffused amongst us. (Jos 21:43-45)

God promised to give to the seed of Abraham the land of Canaan for a possession, and now they possessed it, and dwelt therein. And the promise of the heavenly Canaan is as sure to all God's spiritual Israel; for it is the promise of Him that cannot lie. There stood not a man before them. The after-prevalence of the Canaanites was the effect of Israel's slothfulness, and the punishment of their sinful inclination to the idolatries and abominations of the heathen whom they harboured and indulged. There failed not aught of any good thing, which the Lord had spoken to the house of Israel. In due season all his promises will be accomplished; then will his people acknowledge that the Lord has exceeded their largest expectations, and made them more than conquerors, and brought them to their desired rest.
